title: Eurasian Tree Sparrow
body:
Being back in the streets of Basantapur after 3 years with a camera in hand felt strangely unfamiliar. A place that once never felt strange now felt awkward, almost like I had to relearn how to see it.

After spending time in the States and avoiding street photography for a while, I think some form of public photography anxiety had settled in without me noticing.

Still, this frame reminded me why I keep coming back to photography. The soft bokeh, the proud pose of the bird, and the simplicity of the scene came together in a way I really loved when I revisited the edit.

What makes it even more special is that this image came from a camera that’s about 15 years old, paired with a half-broken lens. Sometimes gear limitations make the result feel even more meaningful.
